presentation.label: CHORD ARP
presentation.summary: Turn a Digitakt II audio trig into a chord played one note at a time.
presentation.overview: Start with a single note trig and choose a chord shape and note order. The trig's NOTE value can set the root, or you can choose a fixed pitch. Shape the phrase with octave limits, rhythm and groove, then use SPAN or LATCH to play through empty steps.
highlights: Chord extensions from the 7th to the 13th
Thirteen note orders and independent octave limits
Per-trig chord, root and rhythm locks
usage: Place a C5 note trig on step 1 of a pitched audio track.
Open SETTINGS, select CHORD ARP, and set TYPE to MAJ and ROOT to TRIG.
Press RIGHT, set ORDER to UP and DIV to 1/16, then turn ARP on.
Press FUNC + RIGHT, turn SPAN on, then press PLAY.

steps: Use LEFT and RIGHT to switch pages. Press NO to return.

load.display: Bounded sequencer work per audio-track step
load.conditions: Source bound: at most 72 pitches in a voicing, six subdivisions per stock step, and eight scheduled notes per phrase. A group edit checks at most 16 held trigs and 32 lock slots in the UI. No per-sample DSP code. Physical CPU percentage was not measured.

hardware.summary: QF17 restored both ARP switches and the checked trig lock on each of two tracks after a save and cold boot, before a manual load. The same Chord Arp binary passed multi-trig editing and clearing on QE17. See TESTING.md for exact package and base identities.
limitations: All 32 slots were checked on reload in Digikit. The physical QF17 cold-boot test checked one locked trig per track.
Opening a QF17-saved project on official OS, project reload alongside Euclidean Scale, and operation alongside Track Names were not tested on this build.
Chord Arp supports audio tracks. MIDI tracks were not tested.

tests.summary: The author verified cold-boot project recall on QF17. Digikit verified all 32 lock slots and the QE17 group editing path.
